Work Queue Systems第 11 章 工作队列系统

— PDF 第 137 页 —

The simplest form of batch processing is a work queue. In a work queue system, there is a batch of work to be performed. Each piece of work is wholly independent of the other and can be processed without any interactions. Generally, the goals of the work queue system are to ensure that each piece of work is processed within a certain amount of time. Workers are scaled up or scaled down to ensure that the work can be handled. An illustration of a generic work queue is shown in Figure 11-1.

批处理最简单的形式就是工作队列。在工作队列系统中，有一批待完成的工作。每一项工作彼此完全独立，无需任何交互即可被处理。通常，工作队列系统的目标是确保每一项工作都在一定时间内被处理完毕。通过对 worker（工作者）进行扩缩容，来保证工作能够被及时处理。图 11-1 给出了一个通用工作队列的示意图。

A Generic Work Queue System通用工作队列系统

The work queue is an ideal way to demonstrate the power of distributed system patterns. Most of the logic in the work queue is wholly independent of the actual work being done, and in many cases the delivery of the work can be performed in an independent manner as well. To illustrate this point, consider the work queue illustrated in Figure 11-1. If we take a look at it again and identify functionality that can be provided by a shared set of library containers, it becomes apparent that most of the implementation of a containerized work queue can be shared across a wide variety of users, as shown in Figure 11-2.

工作队列是展示分布式系统模式威力的理想样例。工作队列中的大部分逻辑与实际所做的工作完全无关；而且在许多情况下，工作的投递也可以独立完成。为说明这一点，请看图 11-1 所示的工作队列。我们再看它一眼，把那些可以由一套共享的“库容器”提供的功能识别出来，就会发现：容器化工作队列的大部分实现都可以被广泛的不同用户所共享，如图 11-2 所示。

— PDF 第 138 页 —

Building a reusable container-based work queue requires the definition of interfaces between the generic library containers and the user-defined application logic. In the containerized work queue, there are two interfaces: the source container interface, which provides a stream of work items that need processing, and the worker container interface, which knows how to actually process a work item.

构建一个可复用的、基于容器的工作队列，需要在通用库容器与用户自定义应用逻辑之间定义接口。在容器化工作队列中，共有两个接口：源容器接口（source container interface）负责提供一串待处理的工作项；worker 容器接口（worker container interface）则知道如何真正处理一个工作项。

The Source Container Interface源容器接口

To operate, every work queue needs a collection of work items that need processing. There are many different sources of work items for the work queue, depending on the specific application of the work queue. However, once the set of items has been obtained, the actual operation of the work queue is quite generic. Consequently, we can separate the application-specific queue source logic from the generic queue processing logic. Given the previously defined patterns of container groups, this can be seen as an example of the ambassador pattern defined previously. The generic work queue container is the primary application container, and the application-specific source container is the ambassador that proxies the generic work queue's requests out to the concrete definition of the work queue out in the real world. This container group is illustrated in Figure 11-3.

工作队列要运转起来，首先需要有一批待处理的工作项。工作项的来源多种多样，取决于工作队列的具体应用。然而，一旦拿到了这批工作项，工作队列的实际操作就相当通用了。因此，我们可以把与应用相关的队列源逻辑，与通用的队列处理逻辑分离开来。结合前面定义过的容器组模式，这可以看作是之前定义过的 ambassador（大使）模式的一个例子：通用工作队列容器是主应用容器，而与应用相关的源容器就是那个 ambassador，它把通用工作队列的请求代理出去，对接现实世界中工作队列的具体定义。这个容器组如图 11-3 所示。

— PDF 第 139 页 —

Interestingly, while the ambassador container is clearly application-specific, there is also a variety of generic implementations of the work queue source API. For example, a source might be a list of pictures stored in a cloud storage API, a collection of files stored on network storage, or a queue in a pub/sub system like Kafka or Redis. In these cases, though the user chooses the particular work queue ambassador that fits their scenario, they should be reusing a single generic “library” implementation of the container itself. This minimizes work and maximizes code reuse.

有趣的是，尽管 ambassador 容器显然是与应用相关的，但工作队列源 API 也存在多种通用实现。例如，一个源可以是存储在云存储 API 中的图片列表，可以是网络存储上的一批文件，也可以是 Kafka 或 Redis 这类发布/订阅系统中的一个队列。在这些情况下，尽管用户会选择适合自己场景的那个特定工作队列 ambassador，但他们应当复用同一个通用的“库”容器实现本身。这样可以把工作量降到最低，把代码复用最大化。

Work Queue API工作队列 API

Given this coordination between the generic work-queue manager and the application-specific ambassador, we need a formal definition of the interface between the two containers. Though there are a variety of different protocols, an HTTP RESTful API is both the easiest to implement as well as the de facto standard for such an interface. The coordinating work queue expects the ambassador to implement the following URLs:

既然通用工作队列管理器与与应用相关的 ambassador 之间需要这样的协作，我们就需要为这两个容器之间的接口给出一个正式定义。尽管协议有很多种，但 HTTP RESTful API 既最容易实现，也是这类接口事实上的标准。负责协调的工作队列要求 ambassador 实现以下 URL：

GET http://localhost/api/v1/items
GET http://localhost/api/v1/items/

You might wonder why we include a v1 in the API definition. Will there ever be a v2 of this interface? It may not seem logical, but it costs very little to version your API when you initially define it. Refactoring versioning onto an API without it, on the other hand, is very expensive. Consequently, it is a best practice to always add versions to your APIs even if you're not sure they will ever change. Better safe than sorry.

你可能会奇怪：为什么我们在 API 定义里要加一个 v1？这个接口将来真的会有 v2 吗？这看起来也许不太合逻辑，但在最初定义 API 时就加上版本号，代价非常小。反过来，事后再给一个没有版本号的 API 补上版本机制，成本就非常高了。因此，即使你不确定 API 将来会不会变，最好的做法也总是给 API 加上版本号。稳妥总比后悔好。

— PDF 第 140 页 —

The /items/ URL returns a complete list of all items:

/items/ 这个 URL 返回所有条目的完整列表：

{
   kind: ItemList,
   apiVersion: v1,
   items: [
      "item-1",
      "item-2",
      ….
   ]
}

The /items/ URL provides the details for a specific item:

/items/ 这个 URL 提供某个特定条目的详情：

{
  kind: Item,
  apiVersion: v1,
  data: {
      "some": "json",
    "object": "here",
  }
}

Importantly, you will notice that this API doesn't have any affordances for recording that a work item has been processed. We could have designed a more complicated API and then pushed more implementation into the ambassador container, but remember, the goal of this effort is to place as much of the generic implementation inside of the generic work queue manager as possible. To that end, the work queue manager itself is responsible for tracking which items have been processed and which items remain to be processed.

重要的是，你会注意到这个 API 并没有提供任何用于记录“某个工作项已被处理”的机制。我们本可以设计一个更复杂的 API，把更多实现推到 ambassador 容器里去，但请记住：我们这么做的目标，是把尽可能多的通用实现放进通用工作队列管理器里。为此，工作队列管理器自身负责跟踪哪些条目已被处理、哪些条目仍待处理。

The item details are obtained from this API, and the item.data field is passed along to the worker interface for processing.

条目的详情通过这个 API 获取，而 item.data 字段会被传给 worker 接口进行处理。

The Worker Container InterfaceWorker 容器接口

Once a particular work item has been obtained by the work queue manager, it needs to be processed by a worker. This is the second container interface in our generic work queue. This container and interface are slightly different than the previous work queue source interface for a few reasons. The first is that it is a one-off API: a single call is made to begin the work, and no other API calls are made throughout the life of the worker container. Secondly, the worker container is not inside a container group with the work queue manager. Instead, it is launched via a container orchestration API and scheduled to its own container group. This means that the work queue manager has to make a remote call to the worker container in order to start work. It also means that we may need to be more careful about security to prevent a malicious user in our cluster from injecting extra work into the system.

一旦工作队列管理器拿到了某个特定工作项，就需要由一个 worker 来处理它。这就是我们通用工作队列中的第二个容器接口。这个容器和接口与前面的工作队列源接口略有不同，原因有几点。第一，它是一个一次性 API：只发起一次调用来启动工作，在 worker 容器的整个生命周期内不再有其他 API 调用。第二，worker 容器并不与工作队列管理器处在同一个容器组里；相反，它是通过容器编排 API 启动、被调度到自己独立的容器组中的。这意味着工作队列管理器必须对 worker 容器发起一次远程调用来启动工作；也意味着我们需要在安全性上更加小心，防止集群里的恶意用户向系统注入额外的工作。

— PDF 第 141 页 —

With the work queue source API, we used a simple HTTP-based API for sending items back to the work queue manager. This was because we needed to make repeated calls to the API, and security wasn't a concern since everything was running on localhost. With the worker container, we only need to make a single call, and we want to ensure that other users in the system can't accidentally or maliciously add work to our workers. Consequently, for the worker container, we will use a file-based API. Namely, when the worker container is created, it will receive an environment variable named WORK_ITEM_FILE; this will point to a file in the container's local filesystem, where the data field from a work item has been written to a file. Concretely, as you will see below, this API can be implemented via a Kubernetes ConfigMap object that can be mounted into a container group as a file, as illustrated in Figure 11-4.

对于工作队列源 API，我们使用了一个简单的、基于 HTTP 的 API 把条目回传给工作队列管理器。这是因为我们需要反复调用该 API，而且由于一切都运行在 localhost 上，安全并不是问题。而对于 worker 容器，我们只需要发起一次调用，并且希望确保系统中的其他用户不会意外或恶意地向我们的 worker 添加工作。因此，对于 worker 容器，我们将使用一个基于文件的 API。具体来说，当 worker 容器被创建时，它会收到一个名为 WORK_ITEM_FILE 的环境变量；该变量指向容器本地文件系统中的一个文件，而某个工作项的 data 字段已经被写入这个文件。具体地，如下文所示，这个 API 可以通过一个 Kubernetes ConfigMap 对象来实现，该对象可以作为文件挂载进容器组，如图 11-4 所示。

This file-based API pattern is also easier for the container to implement. Often a work queue worker is simply a shell script across a few command-line tools. In that context, spinning up a web server to manage the work to perform is an unnecessary complexity. As was true with the work queue source implementation, most of the worker containers will be special-purpose container images built for specific work queue applications, but there are also generic workers that can be applied to multiple different work queue applications.

这种基于文件的 API 模式对容器来说也更容易实现。工作队列 worker 往往就是一个串联了若干命令行工具的 shell 脚本。在这种场景下，为管理待执行的工作而专门拉起一个 Web 服务器，是一种不必要的复杂度。与工作队列源的实现一样，大多数 worker 容器是为特定工作队列应用构建的专用容器镜像，但也存在一些可复用于多个不同工作队列应用的通用 worker。

Consider the example of a work queue worker that downloads a file from cloud storage and runs a shell script with that file as input, and then copies its output back up to cloud storage. Such a container can be mostly generic but then have the specific script to execute supplied to it as a runtime parameter. In this way, most of the work of file handling can be shared by multiple users/work queues and only the specifics of file processing need to be supplied by the end user.

举个例子：有这样一个工作队列 worker，它从云存储下载一个文件，以该文件作为输入运行一个 shell 脚本，再把脚本输出复制回云存储。这样的容器大部分都可以是通用的，只需把要执行的具体脚本作为运行时参数提供给它即可。如此一来，文件处理的大部分工作都可以被多个用户/工作队列共享，只有文件处理的具体细节需要由终端用户提供。

— PDF 第 142 页 —

The Shared Work Queue Infrastructure共享的工作队列基础设施

Given implementations of the two container interfaces described previously, what is left to implement our reusable work queue implementation? The basic algorithm for the work queue is fairly straightforward:

既然前面两个容器接口都已经有了实现，那么要完成我们这个可复用工作队列的实现，还剩下什么？工作队列的基本算法相当直接：

  1. Load the available work by calling into source container interface.调用源容器接口，加载可用的工作。
  2. Consult with work queue state to determine which work items have been processed or are being processed currently.查询工作队列状态，确定哪些工作项已被处理、哪些正在被处理。
  3. For these items, spawn jobs that use the worker container interface to process the work item.为这些条目派生任务（Job），由它们使用 worker 容器接口来处理该工作项。
  4. When one of these worker containers finishes successfully, record that the work item has been completed.当其中某个 worker 容器成功完成时，记录该工作项已完成。

While this algorithm is simple to express in words, it is somewhat more complicated to implement in reality. Fortunately for us, the Kubernetes container orchestrator contains a number of features that make it significantly easier to implement. Namely, Kubernetes contains a Job object that allows for the reliable execution of the work queue. The Job can be configured to either run the worker container once or to run it until it completes successfully. If the worker container is set to run to completion, then even if a machine in the cluster fails, the job will eventually be run to success. This dramatically simplifies the task of building a work queue because the orchestrator takes on responsibility for the reliable operation of each work item. Additionally, Kubernetes has annotations for each Job object that enable us to mark each job with the work item it is processing. This enables us to understand which items are being processed as well as those that have completed in either failure or success.

虽然这个算法用文字表达起来很简单，但实际实现起来要稍微复杂一些。幸运的是，Kubernetes 容器编排器内置了若干特性，让实现这件事变得容易得多。具体来说，Kubernetes 提供了一个 Job 对象，可用于可靠地执行工作队列。Job 可以配置为只运行一次 worker 容器，或者一直运行直到成功完成为止。如果把 worker 容器设置为“运行至完成”，那么即使集群中某台机器故障，该 Job 最终也会被运行到成功。这极大地简化了构建工作队列的任务，因为编排器承担起了每个工作项可靠运行的责任。此外，Kubernetes 为每个 Job 对象提供了注解（annotation），使我们能够给每个任务标记上它正在处理的工作项。这样我们就能知道哪些条目正在被处理，以及哪些条目已经以失败或成功告终。

Put together, this means that we can implement a work queue on top of the Kubernetes orchestration layer without using any storage of our own. Thus, the expanded operation of our work queue container looks like this:

综合起来，这意味着我们可以在 Kubernetes 编排层之上实现一个工作队列，而无需使用任何自己的存储。于是，我们工作队列容器的扩展后运行逻辑如下：

Repeat forever
    Get the list of work items from the work source container interface.
    Get the list of all jobs that have been created to service this work
        queue.
    Difference these lists to find the set of work items that haven't
        been processed.
    For these unprocessed items, create new Job objects that spawn the
        appropriate worker container.

Here is a simple Python script that implements this work queue:

下面是一个实现该工作队列的简单 Python 脚本：

import requests
import json
from kubernetes import client, config
import time

namespace = "default"

def make_container(item, obj):
    container = client.V1Container()
    container.image = "my/worker-image"
    container.name = "worker"
    return container

def make_job(item):
    response = requests.get("http://localhost:8000/items/{}".format(item))
    obj = json.loads(response.text)
    job = client.V1Job()
    job.metadata = client.V1ObjectMeta()
    job.metadata.name = item
    job.spec = client.V1JobSpec()
    job.spec.template = client.V1PodTemplate()
    job.spec.template.spec = client.V1PodTemplateSpec()
    job.spec.template.spec.restart_policy = "Never"
    job.spec.template.spec.containers = [
        make_container(item, obj)
    ]
    return job

def update_queue(batch):
    response = requests.get("http://localhost:8000/items")

    obj = json.loads(response.text)
    items = obj['items']

    ret = batch.list_namespaced_job(namespace, watch=False)

    for item in items:
        found = False
        for i in ret.items:
            if i.metadata.name == item:
                found = True
        if not found:
            # This function creates the job object, omitted for
            # brevity
            job = make_job(item)
            batch.create_namespaced_job(namespace, job)

config.load_kube_config()
batch = client.BatchV1Api()

while True:
    update_queue(batch)
    time.sleep(10)

Hands On: Implementing a Video Thumbnailer动手实践：实现一个视频缩略图生成器

To provide a concrete example of how we might use a work queue, consider the task of generating thumbnails for videos. These thumbnails help users determine which videos they want to watch.

为了具体说明我们如何使用工作队列，请看一个为视频生成缩略图的任务。这些缩略图帮助用户判断自己想看哪个视频。

To implement this video thumbnailer, we need two different user containers. The first is the work item source container. The simplest way for this to work is for the work items to appear on a shared disk, such as a Network File System (NFS) share. The work item source simply lists the files in this directory and returns them to the caller. Here's a simple node program that does this:

要实现这个视频缩略图生成器，我们需要两个不同的用户容器。第一个是工作项源容器。最简单的做法是让工作项出现在一块共享磁盘上，比如网络文件系统（NFS）共享。工作项源只需列出该目录下的文件并返回给调用方。下面是一个实现这件事的简单 node 程序：

const http = require('http');
const fs = require('fs');

const port = 8080;
const path = process.env.MEDIA_PATH;

const requestHandler = (request, response) => {
        console.log(request.url);
        fs.readdir(path + '/*.mp4', (err, items) => {
                var msg = {
                        'kind': 'ItemList',
                        'apiVersion': 'v1',
                        'items': []
                };
                if (!items) {
                        return msg;
                }
                for (var i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
                        msg.items.push(items[i]);
                }
                response.end(JSON.stringify(msg));
        });
}

const server = http.createServer(requestHandler);

server.listen(port, (err) => {
        if (err) {
                return console.log('Error starting server', err);
        }

        console.log(`server is active on ${port}`)
});

This source of defines the queue of movies to thumbnail. We use the ffmpeg utility to actually perform the thumbnailing work.

这个源定义了待生成缩略图的电影队列。我们使用 ffmpeg 工具来真正完成缩略图生成的工作。

— PDF 第 145 页 —

You can create a container that uses the following as its command line:

你可以创建一个容器，把下面这行作为它的命令行：

ffmpeg -i ${INPUT_FILE} -frames:v 100 thumb.png

This command will take one frame every 100 frames (that's the -frames:v 100 flag) and output it as a PNG file (e.g., thumb1.png, thumb2.png, etc.).

这条命令每隔 100 帧抽取一帧（即 -frames:v 100 这个参数），并把它输出为一个 PNG 文件（例如 thumb1.png、thumb2.png 等）。

You can create the ffmpeg container using a base image of your choice and installing the ffmpeg executable in that container. There is also an open source project with Dockerfiles for many popular operating systems on GitHub. You can use those scripts as a starting point for your container image.

你可以用自己选择的基础镜像来创建 ffmpeg 容器，并在其中安装 ffmpeg 可执行文件。GitHub 上还有一个开源项目，为许多主流操作系统提供了 Dockerfile。你可以把这些脚本作为自己容器镜像的起点。

By defining a simple source container as well as an even simpler worker container, we can clearly see the power and utility of a generic container-based queuing system. It dramatically reduces the time/distance between an idea for implementing a work queue and the corresponding concrete implementation.

通过定义一个简单的源容器、以及一个更简单的 worker 容器，我们就能清楚看到一个通用的、基于容器的队列系统的威力与效用。它极大地缩短了“产生实现工作队列的想法”与“拿出相应具体实现”之间的时间与距离。

Dynamic Scaling of the WorkersWorker 的动态扩缩容

The previously described work queue is great for processing work items as quickly as they arrive in the work queue, but this can lead to bursty resource loads being placed onto a container orchestrator cluster. This is good if you have a lot of different workloads that will burst at different times and thus keep your infrastructure evenly utilized. But if you don't have a sufficient number of different workloads, this feast or famine approach to scaling your work queue might require that you over-provision resources to support the bursts that will lie idle (and cost too much money) while you don't have work to perform.

前面描述的工作队列非常适合“工作项一进队列就尽快处理”，但这会给容器编排集群带来突发式的资源负载。如果你有大量不同的工作负载、它们在不同时间点突发，从而让基础设施得到均衡利用，那这很好。但如果你没有足够多的不同工作负载，这种“饱一顿饥一顿”的扩缩容方式可能会让你过度预置资源来支撑突发——而在你没有工作要做时，这些资源又会闲置（并浪费大量金钱）。

To address this problem, you can limit the overall number of Job objects that your work queue is willing to create. This will naturally serve to limit the number of work items you process in parallel and consequentially limit the maximum amount of resources that you use at a particular time. However, doing this will increase the time to completion (latency) for each work item being completed when under heavy load. If the load is bursty, then this is probably OK because you can use the slack times to catch up with the backlog that developed during a burst of usage. However, if your steady-state usage is too high, your work queue may never be able to catch up, and the time to completion will simply get longer and longer.

为解决这个问题，你可以限制工作队列愿意创建的 Job 对象总数。这自然会限制你并行处理的工作项数量，从而限制你在某一时刻使用的资源上限。然而，这样做会在高负载下增加每个工作项被完成所需的时间（延迟）。如果负载是突发式的，这大概还可以接受，因为你可以利用空闲时间把突发期间积压的工作补回来。但如果你的稳态使用率过高，工作队列可能永远也追不上，完成时间只会越来越长。

When your work queue is faced with this situation, you need to have it dynamically adjust itself to increase the parallelism that it is willing to create (and correspondingly the resources it is willing to use) so that it can keep up with the incoming work. Fortunately, there are mathematical formulas that we can use to determine when we need to dynamically scale up our work queue.

当工作队列面临这种局面时，你需要让它动态调整自身，提高它愿意创建的并行度（以及相应愿意使用的资源），以便跟上涌入的工作。幸运的是，我们可以用一些数学公式来判断何时需要动态扩容工作队列。

— PDF 第 146 页 —

Consider a work queue where a new work item arrives an average of once every minute, and each work item takes an average of 30 seconds to complete. Such a system is capable of keeping up with all of the work it receives. Even if a large batch of work arrives all at once and creates a backlog, on average the work queue processes two work items for every one work item that arrives, and thus it will be able to gradually work through its backlog.

设想这样一个工作队列：平均每分钟到达一个新工作项，而每个工作项平均需要 30 秒完成。这样的系统能够跟上它收到的所有工作。即使一大批工作一次性到达、造成积压，平均而言工作队列每收到一个工作项就能处理两个，因此它能够逐步把积压的工作消化掉。

If, instead, a new work item arrives on average once every minute and it takes an average of one minute to process each work item, then the system is perfectly balanced, but it does not handle variance well. It can catch up with bursts—but it will take a while, and it has no slack or capacity to absorb a sustained increase in the rate at which new work items arrive. This is probably not an ideal way to run, as some safety margin for growth and other sustained increases in work (or unexpected slowdowns in processing) is needed to preserve a stable system.

反过来，如果平均每分钟到达一个新工作项，而每个工作项平均需要一分钟处理，那么系统恰好处于平衡状态，但它对波动的应对能力很差。它能追赶上突发——但要花上一阵时间，而且它没有任何余量或能力来吸收新工作项到达速率的持续增长。这大概不是一种理想的运行方式，因为要维持一个稳定的系统，就需要为增长、以及其他持续增加的工作（或处理过程中意外的变慢）保留一定的安全余量。

Finally, consider a system in which a work item arrives every minute and each item takes two minutes to process. In such a system, we are always losing ground. The queue of work will grow without bound, and the latency of any one item in the queue will grow toward infinity (and our users will become very frustrated).

最后，设想这样一个系统：每分钟到达一个工作项，而每个项需要两分钟处理。在这样的系统里，我们永远在节节败退。工作队列会无限制地增长，队列中任意一个项的延迟都会趋向于无穷大（而我们的用户会变得非常恼火）。

Thus, we can keep track of both of these metrics for our work queue, and the average time between work items over an extended period of time (# work items / 24 hours) will give us the interarrival time for new work. We can also keep track of the average latency, the time to process any one item once we start working on it, not counting any time spent waiting in the queue. To have a stable work queue, we need to adjust the number of resources so that latency is less than the interarrival time of new items. If we are processing work items in parallel, we also divide the processing time for a work item by the parallelism. For example, if each item takes one minute to process but we process four items in parallel, the effective time to process one item is 15 seconds, and thus we can sustain an interarrival period of 16 or more seconds.

因此，我们可以为工作队列跟踪这两个指标：长时间内工作项之间的平均间隔时间（# 工作项 / 24 小时）会给出新工作的到达间隔（interarrival time）；我们还可以跟踪平均延迟，即一旦开始处理某个项、处理它所花的时间（不包括在队列中等待的时间）。要拥有一个稳定的工作队列，我们需要调整资源数量，使延迟小于新项的到达间隔。如果我们是并行处理工作项，还要把单个工作项的处理时间除以并行度。例如，如果每个项需要一分钟处理、但我们并行处理四个项，那么处理一个项的有效时间就是 15 秒，于是我们就能承受 16 秒或更长的到达间隔。

This approach makes it fairly straightforward to build an autoscaler to dynamically size up our work queue. Sizing down the work queue is somewhat trickier, but you can use the same math as well as a heuristic for the amount of spare capacity for the safety margin you want to maintain. For example, you can reduce the parallelism until the processing time for an item is 90% of the interarrival time for new items. While in some cases it is more efficient to build your own scaler, many times it is better to use an open source solution. That is where the Kubernetes Event-Driven Autoscaling (KEDA) project is useful. KEDA provides numerous different event-based scalers, which can be used to scale your application. KEDA supports event sources ranging from files on disk to events in pub/sub systems and many more.

这种思路让构建一个自动扩缩容器、动态地为工作队列扩容变得相当直接。缩容工作队列要稍微棘手一些，但你可以使用同样的数学，再加上一个关于“希望保留多少富余容量作为安全余量”的启发式规则。例如，你可以降低并行度，直到单个项的处理时间达到新项到达间隔的 90%。虽然在某些情况下自己写扩缩容器更高效，但很多时候使用开源方案会更好。这时 Kubernetes Event-Driven Autoscaling（KEDA）项目就派上用场了。KEDA 提供了众多不同的、基于事件的扩缩器（scaler），可用于扩缩你的应用。KEDA 支持的事件源范围很广，从磁盘上的文件到发布/订阅系统中的事件等等。

— PDF 第 147 页 —

The Multiworker Pattern多 Worker 模式

One of the themes of this book has been the use of containers for encapsulation and reuse of code. The same holds true for the work queue patterns described in this chapter. In addition to the patterns for reusing containers for driving the work queue itself, you can also reuse multiple different containers to compose a worker implementation. Suppose, for example, that you have three different types of work that you want to perform on a particular work queue item. For example, you might want to detect faces in an image, tag those faces with identities, and then blur the faces in the image. You could write a single worker to perform this complete set of tasks, but this would be a bespoke solution that would not be reusable the next time you want to identify something else, such as cars, yet still provide the same blurring.

本书的主题之一，就是用容器来封装和复用代码。本章描述的工作队列模式也是如此。除了用可复用容器来驱动工作队列本身的那些模式之外，你还可以复用多个不同的容器，来组合出一个 worker 实现。举个例子，假设你想对某个特定工作队列项执行三种不同类型的工作。比如，你可能想检测一张图片中的人脸、用身份信息给这些人脸打标签，然后再把图片中的人脸模糊掉。你可以写一个 worker 来完成这一整套任务，但那会是一个定制方案；下一次你想识别别的东西（比如汽车）、同时仍提供相同的模糊处理时，它就无法复用了。

To achieve this kind of code reuse, the multiworker pattern is something of a specialization of the adapter pattern described in previous chapters. In this case, the multiworker pattern transforms a collection of different worker containers into a single unified container that implements the worker interface, yet delegates the actual work to a collection of different reusable containers. This process is illustrated in Figure 11-5.

为了实现这种代码复用，多 worker 模式可以看作是前面章节所述适配器（adapter）模式的一种特化。在这种情况下，多 worker 模式把一组不同的 worker 容器，变换成一个实现了 worker 接口的统一容器，但它把实际工作委托给一组不同的可复用容器。这个过程如图 11-5 所示。

Because of this code reuse, the composition of multiple different worker containers means an increase in the reuse of code and a reduction in effort for people designing batch-oriented distributed systems.

由于这种代码复用，把多个不同 worker 容器组合起来，意味着代码复用率提高，也减少了设计面向批处理的分布式系统的人们所需付出的工作量。

— PDF 第 148 页 —

Summary小结

This chapter begins the discussion of batch systems by introducing workflows. A workflow is a sequence of discrete actions which, when put together in a sequence, achieve some goal like the processing of an order or the machine-learning analysis of a video. This chapter showed how containers can be used to build modular workflows with sidecar containers providing workflow orchestration while application containers supply the specific processing necessary for your workflow. Workflow is a key part of most distributed batch systems. Its generic pattern is easy to adapt and extend to meet the specific needs of your workload.

本章通过引入工作流（workflow）开始对批处理系统的讨论。工作流是一系列离散动作，按顺序组合在一起时，就能达成某个目标，比如处理一个订单，或对一段视频做机器学习分析。本章展示了如何用容器构建模块化的工作流：由边车容器提供工作流编排，而应用容器提供工作流所需的具体处理。工作流是大多数分布式批处理系统的关键组成部分。它的通用模式很容易适配和扩展，以满足你的工作负载的具体需求。
